title: Don't Miss a Thing With 'Eagle Eyes'
attribution: Audio: VOA Learning English (learningenglish.voanews.com), dominio público
transcriptSummary: This episode explains idioms about vision and attention, such as 'bird's eye view' and 'eagle eyes'. It describes how a bird's eye view means seeing the big picture from above, while having 'eagle eyes' means noticing small details that others miss. The host gives everyday examples of using both expressions when starting a project or reviewing work carefully.

title: Sometimes We 'Spread Ourself Too Thin'
attribution: Audio: VOA Learning English (learningenglish.voanews.com), dominio público
transcriptSummary: This episode discusses the idiom 'spread yourself too thin', meaning to take on too many responsibilities at once (family, work, community, personal projects). It explains related expressions like 'having a lot on your plate' and 'overextended', and talks about the feeling of being pushed to the limit when trying to do too much.

title: The Importance of Being 'Dialed In'
attribution: Audio: VOA Learning English (learningenglish.voanews.com), dominio público
transcriptSummary: This episode explores the origin of the expression 'dialed in', which comes from old mechanical dials and controls on electronic devices. It explains how the phrase now means being highly focused, prepared, and attentive to a task, and gives examples of using it in daily conversation and at work.

title: 'Kitchen-Table' Is a Type of Politics
attribution: Audio: VOA Learning English (learningenglish.voanews.com), dominio público
transcriptSummary: This episode explains the expression 'kitchen-table politics', describing issues that directly affect everyday family life, like the cost of groceries or healthcare, as opposed to abstract political debates. It notes the kitchen table as the center of the home where families discuss daily concerns, and compares this to other types of everyday political language.

title: What Does It Take to Be a 'Power Couple'?
attribution: Audio: VOA Learning English (learningenglish.voanews.com), dominio público
transcriptSummary: This episode covers English expressions describing close relationships and similarities between people: 'joined at the hip', 'thick as thieves', 'two peas in a pod', and 'kindred spirits'. It explains what each phrase means, gives usage examples, and discusses how the term 'power couple' describes two accomplished, closely connected people.

title: How to Lower Your Risk of Dementia Starting in Middle Age
attribution: Audio: VOA Learning English (learningenglish.voanews.com), dominio público
transcriptSummary: This report discusses a large U.S. study suggesting the lifetime risk of developing dementia is higher than previously thought, especially after age 75. It explains that people over 55 face up to a 42 percent chance of developing the disease if they live long enough, but notes that controlling blood pressure and other health steps can reduce that risk.

title: Saying 'No' at Work Can Be Good for Your Health
attribution: Audio: VOA Learning English (learningenglish.voanews.com), dominio público
transcriptSummary: This report explains why workplace experts recommend learning to set limits and say 'no' to protect physical and mental health. It follows Justin Stewart, a young production assistant who used to work multiple jobs and struggled with boundaries, and describes how setting limits gets easier with practice and helps prevent burnout.

title: How Physical Therapists Can Prevent Future Health Problems
attribution: Audio: VOA Learning English (learningenglish.voanews.com), dominio público
transcriptSummary: This report describes how physical therapists can do more than treat injuries after surgery or accidents — they can also help identify and prevent future health problems through regular visits. It features comments from physical therapy association leaders who describe therapists as an underused resource in preventive health care.
